name: Ipratropium bromide
executiveSummary: Short-acting inhaled anticholinergic (SAMA). Adult neb attack: **500 µg q6–8h** (± salbutamol). MDI: **2 puffs (40 µg) q6–8h** (max ~12 puffs/day). Pediatric neb: **250–500 µg** q6–8h (infants **125–250 µg**).
indications:
## Indications

- Bronchospasm in COPD/asthma (add-on to SABA in attacks).
- Rhinorrhea (nasal spray some brands).

## Precautions

- Avoid eye contact (mydriasis, angle-closure glaucoma).
- Caution in BPH / urinary retention.
- Not first-line asthma controller (prefer ICS ± LABA).

> Severe asthma attack: combine with salbutamol in neb.

adulto.presentation: Neb solution 250–500 µg/2 mL; MDI 20 µg/puff; nasal spray by brand.
adulto.dose: Neb: **500 µg q6–8h** (in attacks often with salbutamol q20min × 3). MDI: **2 puffs (40 µg) q6–8h**; usual max **12 puffs/day**.
adulto.administration: Nebulized or MDI (+ spacer). Avoid mist in eyes.
adulto.notes: Fixed ipratropium+salbutamol combos follow product label.

pediatrico.dose: Neb: neonates/infants **25 µg/kg** or **125–250 µg** q8h; children **250–500 µg** q6–8h. MDI 3–14 y: **1–2 puffs** up to 3×/day (max ~6 puffs/day per label).
pediatrico.notes: Monitor HR if high-dose salbutamol co-administered.

stability:
## Stability

- Neb ampoules: use after opening; dilute in NS if protocol requires.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dry mouth, cough, headache; rare: urinary retention, mydriasis/glaucoma, allergy.
